must_remember: The Carnot cycle consists of four reversible processes: two isothermal and two adiabatic.
The thermal efficiency of a Carnot engine is given by $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_2}{T_1}$, where $T_1$ and $T_2$ are absolute temperatures.
Carnot's theorem states that no heat engine can be more efficient than a reversible Carnot engine operating between the same two temperatures.
The efficiency of a Carnot engine is completely independent of the nature of the working substance.
The Coefficient of Performance (COP) of an ideal refrigerator is given by $\beta = \frac{T_2}{T_1 - T_2} = \frac{1 - \eta}{\eta}$.

glossary.meaning: The higher temperature of the thermal reservoir from which heat is absorbed by the working substance.
The lower temperature of the thermal reservoir to which unused heat is rejected.
The ratio of heat extracted from the cold reservoir to the work done on the refrigerator.
A thermodynamic process that can be reversed without leaving any change in the system or surroundings.
